answer: Behavioral canyon clustering. Agents log each transaction's timing, value, and counterparty into a feature space; a mixture model fits clusters, and any dense nebula of near-identical behavioral profiles gets flagged post hoc. Flagged identities lose accumulated reputation and future fee rebates. An attacker must give each sybil a genuinely distinct behavior pattern, raising per-identity cost through extra coordination and reduced automation, and any slip onto a shared knoll of sameness collapses the whole cluster.
